items.title: Vertical vs Horizontal Scaling
items.spoken_hook: Traffic बढ़े तो server बड़ा करोगे, या servers बढ़ाओगे?
facts_to_verify: Vertical adds resources to same machine; horizontal adds instances. Capacity figures explicitly illustrative and ideal, shared bottleneck and loss of one replica caveats stated.

items.title: How a Load Balancer Routes Requests
items.spoken_hook: Three servers हैं, user की request किस पर जाएगी?
items.hook_source: Floor roadmap and existing owner teaching rules
facts_to_verify: AWS ALB documentation supports request distribution to registered targets, health monitoring, and periodic configured checks. The example has A/C healthy and B failing; no universal all-targets-unhealthy behavior or zero-error guarantee is asserted. In fact, narration states product/policy dependence when all are unhealthy. Reverse-proxy return path is identified as that setup. 3*100=300 and loss to 200 are ideal illustrative capacity arithmetic, explicitly requiring a load test.

items.title: Round Robin vs Least Connections
items.spoken_hook: A पर six connections हैं, B पर one और C पर three।
items.hook_source: Floor roadmap and existing owner teaching rules
facts_to_verify: NGINX documentation supports round-robin assignments and least-active-connection selection. Equal weights and healthy servers are stated assumptions. Own simulation verifies A/B/C/A/B/C gives two assignments each; for active snapshot6/1/3 and next pointer A, RR chooses A and LC chooses B, incrementing B to2. Counts are illustrative. Fewer connections is a proxy, not a guarantee of CPU load or fastest response. Weights/tie rules are not generalized.
